text.p: Italy's welfare state has to be reformed but any changes should not involve a cut to overall spending, Fausto Bertinotti, the leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation said on Sunday.

In a break with previous policy statements, Bertinotti told a Refoundation convention that he might be prepared to see alterations to the cumbersome state pension system, but again insisted that total pension spending could not be reduced.
"This welfare state is undefendable and will be reformed," Bertinotti said. "But this reform should not be confused for a policy of cuts," he added.
"We need more funds for the health service and education and we must reassure pensioners who receive around a million lire a month or less that they will not be hit," he said.
"However we can intervene, if need be, on excessive pensions and on the scandalously privileged," he continued.

The centre-left government is due to start negotiations with unions and employers on June 18 over welfare reform, with many economists calling for an overhaul of the pension system to keep state accounts in order.
Bertinotti said the question of pension reform should not be discussed until last and added that negotiations between the various parties should be suspended between mid-July and September.
"The talks cannot go on while the workers go on holiday," the hard-left leader said.

Communist Refoundation lies outside the government coalition but guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament. The party has threatened to bring down Prime Minister Romano Prodi if he tries to cut back on social spending.

Analysts say the Italian welfare state is unbalanced, with too much money being channeled into pensions and very little earmarked for young families or youth unemployment. ((-- Rome newsroom +396 6782501))
